typical_symptoms: Water-soaked circular spots on developing cotton bolls
Dark brown to black sunken lesions on boll carpels
Premature boll shedding or defective boll opening
Co-occurrence with angular leaf spots and stem black arm lesions
visual_characteristics: Dark green water-soaked spots on green boll tissue
Sunken, dark brown to reddish-black necrotic patches on fruit
Greasy or shiny surface texture on early lesions
Dark speckling and mottled necrotic areas on immature bolls
lesion_characteristics: Sizes ranging from small 2-5 mm speckles to large coalesced patches
color_characteristics: Progressing to reddish-brown, dark chocolate brown, and jet black
Yellowish to reddish-brown lint staining inside affected bolls
spatial_patterns: Scattered individual spots across carpel walls
Clustered near bract attachments and carpel sutures
Coalescing into large irregular necrotic zones
distinguishing_features: Characteristic water-soaked 'greasy' lesion margins on young bolls
Absence of external fluffy fungal mycelium in early primary bacterial infection
Strong association with angular (vein-bounded) leaf lesions on the same plant
commonly_confused_with: Stink bug feeding punctures and internal boll rot
